title: Book Two · Chapter 122: A Longer Game
story:
The afternoons grow cooler. One Friday, Leo brings a new soft ball to the square. Ronan brings water. Jun arrives with two other boys.

They make two small teams. There are no fine lines on the ground, so Jun uses two leaves to mark one end.

“Do not kick the goal away,” he says.

Leo taps a leaf with his shoe. “This goal is very weak.”

“It costs less than your ball.”

Ronan laughs. Jun looks at him and smiles for a second. Then the game begins.

Leo points to Ronan, then to the nearer goal.

“This side.”

Ronan nods. Jun and the other boys move toward the far end.

They have played so many games in different pairs that Ronan keeps looking toward Jun out of habit. Jun knows the little space he likes near the wall.

Today, that space belongs to the other team.

Leo moves a leaf back beside the goal. One of the other boys asks how wide the opening should be. Jun shows him with two steps.

Ronan waits with his hands against his knees. He can see Leo beside him. He can see Jun farther away.

Then the ball moves.

For the first few moments, all the names and sides are clear. Ronan follows Leo, turns at the wall, and sees Jun run into the open space.

It is a familiar run. He moves before he thinks about the leaf goal behind him.

Ronan runs faster than he expects. He reaches the ball before Leo and sends it toward Jun. Jun turns and scores between the leaves.

“Wrong team,” Leo calls.

Ronan stops. Jun bends with his hands on his knees.

“Thank you,” Jun says. “Very kind.”

The boys laugh. Ronan bows with one hand across his stomach.

“A special service.”

On the next turn, he looks up before he kicks. His own teammate is near the wall. The ball reaches him, and they get a goal back.

They play until the square grows dark. Everybody drinks from a separate cup or bottle. Ronan has forgotten his cup. He pours a little water into his own bottle cap and drinks.

Jun sits on the wall at the other end.

“The reading task today was hard,” one boy says.

“The second question,” Jun says. “The answer was on the back.”

Ronan keeps the bottle in his lap. He knows that question. He could join the talk. He wants to ask Jun about their next task too.

Leo asks Jun about the game instead.

“Same teams next week?”

“Maybe. I have something at home first.”

“Tell us when you know.”

Jun nods. The talk moves to the two leaf goals. One is broken now. The other is under Leo's shoe.

After the others leave, Ronan helps Jun collect the empty bottles from the wall.

“That was a good goal,” Ronan says.

“You gave me a good ball.”

“Not on purpose.”

“I know. It still counts.”

They walk to the edge of the square. Jun turns toward his home.

“About the next reading page—” Ronan begins.

Jun stops.

Ronan looks at his face. Leo is farther along the path with the ball under his arm. Ronan looks toward him.

“Nothing. See you Monday.”

“See you.”

At home, Mum sees the dust on Ronan's knees. She gives him a cloth before he reaches the chair.

“Did you win?”

“Once for the other side.”

“Useful boy.”

Ronan laughs and wipes his legs. He is hungry enough to eat before he tells the rest.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

team＝队；goal＝进球；on purpose＝故意地；count＝算数。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan第一个进球帮了哪队？
2. Jun愿意玩球是否等于愿意重新搭档？

## 读句子

**Jun / turns / toward his home.** Jun／转向／自己家的方向。
